1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3.name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation, Three Knights Variation
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3.strategy: The natural developing move: the knight watches the centre and keeps every plan open, from a fianchetto to a central pawn break. White completes the symmetrical set-up and leaves Black to decide how sharp the game becomes.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3.name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation, Fianchetto Variation
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3.strategy: Prepares to bring the bishop to the long diagonal before the knight is committed, so White can wait and see what Black does in the centre. The game stays flexible and manoeuvring: sound and patient, with Black free to choose between a quick central strike and quiet development.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.e3.strategy: Opens the f1-bishop and supports a later d-pawn push, but it neither stakes out space nor watches d5, so Black can take the central squares at once. Solid and unambitious: White waits for the opponent to show a plan.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5.strategy: Strikes in the centre before White's bishop has even landed, and offers to trade the d-pawn for the c-pawn. Black gets a centralised knight and an easy game, while White aims the bishop and the c3-knight at that knight.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 Nc6.strategy: Develops a piece and adds a second guard of d4, so White cannot easily open the centre with a pawn. Black keeps the pawn break on d5 in reserve and answers White's fianchetto with patient, flexible development.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 g6.strategy: Mirrors White's plan: the bishop will take the long diagonal, pressing on the centre and the c3 knight once the f6 knight moves. Black delays any commitment in the centre, so the game is slower and manoeuvring, and a central break by White has to be met with care.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.cxd5.strategy: Removes the pawn that attacks c4 and prepares to meet the recapture with pressure down the long diagonal. The exchange gives Black a central knight but also a target: once the bishop arrives, d5 is attacked twice.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.Nxd5.strategy: Trades knights and pawns at once for a simple, level game. Black's queen recaptures on d5 and stands actively in the centre, so White has resolved the tension but asked Black no question.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.Bg2.strategy: Completes the fianchetto but ignores the tension in the centre: Black pushes ...d4, hitting the c3 knight and gaining space with tempo. White's position is sound, since the knight has squares, but Black takes the initiative.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5.strategy: The practically forced recapture: the knight returns to the centre. Black hopes to keep a compact set-up around it, but it will soon be hit by both White's knight and bishop and must decide whether to retreat or to trade.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.cxd5 Qxd5.strategy: Recaptures with the queen on a square the c3 knight attacks: Nxd5 wins the queen for a knight, because the f6 knight can only take back a piece of lesser value.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.cxd5 e6.strategy: Offers the pawn to open lines for the c8-bishop: after dxe6 Bxe6 Black has quick development but is a pawn down with no clear compensation. A gambit the position does not justify when a simple recapture is available.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5..strategy: Puts the bishop on the long diagonal, where it attacks d5 a second time. The knight is now hit by bishop and knight and guarded only by the queen, so Black has to answer at once and White gains time.

Develops the king's knight before the bishop and shuts the diagonal from d5 to h1, so a black queen on d5 could not hit the corner rook. White keeps the pressure on the d5 knight and the fianchetto in reserve, for a calm, flexible game.

Removes the centralised knight, but the queen recaptures to an active central square, and the natural Bg2 then hangs the bishop to it, since g2 is unguarded. White has to develop the knight first, and Black has the easier game.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5..name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation, Rubinstein Variation
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.g3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5..strategy: Steps out of the double attack while still guarding d5, and prepares a wall of pawns on c5 and e5 against White's d-pawn. The retreat costs time, but Black's structure is sound and meets the long-diagonal bishop with a solid centre.

Steps out of the double attack while still guarding d5, with the knight also watching c4. Black keeps a compact set-up and can build a pawn wall in the centre, at the price of a tempo lost on the retreat.
Trades the attacked knight instead of retreating it. After bxc3 White has a broad pawn centre and the g2 bishop sees b7 down an open diagonal; Black's position is sound but passive.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 Nc6.strategy: Develops the knight and adds a second guard of d4, so White cannot easily take the centre with a pawn. The structure stays symmetrical and flexible: a patient game of piece play in which both sides choose their moment to break in the centre.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5.strategy: Strikes at the centre at once and offers to trade the d-pawn for White's c-pawn. Black gets a knight on d5 and easy development; the price is that the symmetry is gone and White has a target to aim at.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 e5.name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 e5.strategy: Grabs space with pawns on c5 and e5 that control d4, but fixes the structure: no black pawn can easily challenge a knight on d5 again, so White can settle there and only a piece trade removes it. Playable, but committal.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 e6.strategy: Opens the f8-bishop and supports a later ...d5, while keeping the choice between a central strike and a compact, patient set-up. Black commits to little; the cost is that the c8-bishop is hemmed in for the moment.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5.strategy: Settles the tension in the centre at once: White removes the pawn that attacks c4 and, once Black recaptures, can attack the knight on d5 with the knight on c3. The simplest way to a healthy game, trading a flank pawn for a central one.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.e3.strategy: Opens the f1-bishop and supports a later d-pawn push, but lets Black push ...d4 at once, hitting the c3 knight and gaining space. White has to give ground or trade, so the quiet set-up costs the initiative.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.Nxd5.strategy: Trades knights and pawns immediately and heads for a level game. Black's queen recaptures on d5 and is active in the centre, so White simplifies but gains no edge.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5.strategy: Recaptures with the knight, which develops and in turn attacks the knight on c3. The piece is centralised but also a target, so White can challenge it at once; Black accepts that for easy development and a firm hold on the centre.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5 Qxd5.strategy: Recaptures with the queen on a square the c3 knight attacks: Nxd5 wins the queen for a knight, because the f6 knight can only take back a piece of lesser value.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5 e6.strategy: Offers the pawn to open lines for the c8-bishop: after dxe6 Bxe6 Black has quick development but is a pawn down with no clear compensation. A gambit the position does not justify when a simple recapture is available.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.strategy: Opens the f1-bishop and prepares to challenge the centre with a pawn push on d4. It shuts in the c1-bishop for now and does not rush at the d5 knight: White wants a solid game and a pawn break later.

Prepares to fianchetto the bishop but gives up the fight for the centre: Black keeps the strong knight on d5 and the larger share of space. White must rely on long-diagonal pressure and slow manoeuvring, which is sound but the passive way to treat the position.
Takes the centre with a tempo on the d5 knight and claims the most space. The price is a looser, more open position in which White's king stays in the middle for a while, so the game turns sharp.
Strikes at the centre at once, aiming for a broad pawn centre if Black trades on c3 and open lines for the pieces if it does not. Active play for both sides, with White the one setting the pace.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.name: English Opening: Anglo-Indian Defence
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.strategy: Supports the knight on d5 with a pawn and opens the diagonal of the f8-bishop. The c8-bishop is shut in for the time being, so Black aims for a compact, solid game and relies on piece play rather than space.
Develops a piece, adds pressure on d4 and b4, and keeps the c8-bishop's diagonal open. The d5 knight remains the centre of attention, and Black's pawn structure stays flexible.

Trades the centralised knight before it can be harassed. White recaptures with a broad pawn centre but a ragged queenside, or lets the queens come off; either way the game is simple and level with little for Black to play for.

Develops a piece and adds a second guard of d4, so White cannot easily challenge the centre with a pawn. Black enjoys the extra space White has allowed, at the price of a slower game in which the d5 knight can come under pressure.
Steps back before the fianchetto bishop arrives while still covering d5 and c4. Black keeps a compact set-up and can build a wall of pawns in the centre, at the cost of a tempo.

Trades the centralised knight before the g2 bishop can add to the pressure. After bxc3 White has a broad pawn centre; after dxc3 the queens come off. Simple and level, with little for Black to play for.
Completes the kingside fianchetto and prepares to castle. White's own knight on f3 still stands in the bishop's way, so for the moment only the c3-knight presses on d5, and White is content to wait.
Trades the strong knight, but the queen recaptures to a central square. White gives up the pressure that makes the fianchetto attractive and Black gets an easy, comfortable game.
Builds a solid pawn base and prepares a central pawn break, but shuts in the c1-bishop and adds nothing to the pressure on d5. Black's knight keeps its post and can be traded when it suits.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.name: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation, Rubinstein Variation
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 c5 3.Nf3 d5 4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.strategy: The retreat that defines this set-up: the knight leaves d5 before a trade could pull the queen onto the long diagonal. From c7 it still guards d5 and makes room for a solid wall of pawns on c5 and e5 that holds down d4. The price is time.
Steps back before the knight can be harassed, still covering d5 and c4. Black keeps a compact set-up and can build a wall of pawns in the centre, at the cost of a tempo.
Trades the knight instead of retreating it. After bxc3 White has a broad pawn centre but a ragged queenside; after dxc3 the queens come off. Sound, but passive.
